title: The '20th Century Gabriel' name and the broadcasts
summary: An NBC announcer coined the name and Hawkins did coast-to-coast broadcasts, including from the Lincoln Hotel.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: And when did they start talking about you as the "20th Century Gabriel"?

I was in the Savoy Ballroom doing an NBC broadcast. And, this was in the afternoon. And, the announcer at that time, he brought us on. I had this tune, "Swing Out", composed by Avery Parrish, you know. I had a kind of cadenza like that I played before the tune started swinging. So, when I started playing it slow, taking the time, the announcer happened to hit it upon himself, "The 20th Century Gabriel" coming from the Savoy Ballroom. You know, Erskine Hawkins. And from that time on, everybody, the name just stuck with me. The office, [RCA] Victor started putting it on the records. That way,

the office, they said we'll keep that. And every time I'd broadcast, I used to do a lot of broadcasting. I used to do it like 2 or 3 times a week, my own coast to coast broadcast on ABC, NBC, and CBS.

Then, I'd also, I don't know if I said anything about it, the Blue Room at the Lincoln Hotel? That was during the time before I went into the Strand. I did 14 weeks of broadcasting out there like all over the local stations in the evening. And then, once or twice a week, ABC, CBS, and NBC, they used to follow each other half-hour broadcast coast to coast. I jumped from one to the other so I'd go to coast to coast. And I did that for about 12 weeks or 14 weeks straight at one time.
That's when I'm in the Lincoln. I used to play in the Lincoln a lot when I wasn't in the Savoy.
